issuer.regulator: None — no regulated entity, licence or jurisdiction is disclosed
issuer.summary: Alto Foundation launched DUSD on Ethereum mainnet on 2025-12-10 and has run it without incident since. No team members, legal entity or jurisdiction are disclosed anywhere on the website, documentation or launch materials; contracts are authored under the tag "GPM" with a contact address of security@altofoundation.org, and the seven signers who control the protocol are unidentified. Against that anonymity sits genuinely good security practice: ten external audit engagements across three independent firms — Cantina (four), Enigma Dark (three) and Bailsec (two), plus one further Enigma Dark review — covering the DUSD token itself and the stability module, published in a public repository rather than merely asserted, alongside a bug bounty live since 2025-12-11 paying up to $100,000 for critical findings. ⚠️ Those reports have been indexed but NOT read, so whether their findings were resolved is not established here and the audits must not be described as clean. Operational conduct matches the public account: the Frax partnership is real and verifiable on-chain, the market set has been actively managed from 8 minters at launch to 17 with 50 ceiling changes, and a v2 mint-market implementation was deployed with v1 wound down to dust. The judgement is that this is a competent, transparent-about-code, opaque-about-people issuer with nine months of clean operation and no legal recourse for a holder.
facts: Launched on Ethereum mainnet 2025-12-10; measured clean through 2026-09-21, no incident found and no pause ever fired (Paused has zero emissions on the token)
⚠️ No team members, legal entity, jurisdiction or bankruptcy-remoteness disclosed; seven controlling signers unidentified and not researched

Ten published external audit engagements: Cantina (Jun 2026 lending/liquidations/PSM; Apr 2026 vault; Feb 2026 lending; Dec 2025 oracles/DUSD/vesting; Nov 2025 PSM), Bailsec (Nov 2025 staking; Nov 2025 lending/leverage), Enigma Dark (Nov 2025 multi-component; Sep 2025 rewards; Jul 2025 lending) — github.com/altomoney/security-review-engagements
⚠️ The audit reports were indexed, NOT read. Unresolved-findings status is not established and the audits must not be called clean
Bug bounty live 2025-12-11: critical $20,000–$100,000 capped at 10% of affected funds, high $5,000–$20,000, medium $3,000 flat
The stability module is an acknowledged fork of Aave's GHO GSM (@author Adapted from Aave), inheriting a codebase with far more adversarial exposure than a nine-month-old protocol could generate

Frax partnership verifiable on-chain: frxUSD whitelisted into Alto's permissioned PSM and the DUSD/frxUSD Curve pool launched jointly, with frxUSD's underlying yield flowing to LPs — on-chain state matches the published description exactly

⚠️ A stale public surface: the 2025-12-10 launch post still describes "1:1 swaps with USDC (minus a 0.20% fee)". That USDC module now holds $0.01 with zero available liquidity; the live module is frxUSD at zero fee and permissioned since inception. Alto's later Frax material describes it accurately as a permissioned PSM, so this is staleness rather than misrepresentation — but the launch post is what a holder is most likely to find

Peg history measured over the token's entire life: 283 daily archive samples, worst reading 0.999673 (~3bps). ⚠️ CoinGecko's listed all-time low of $0.9717 on 2026-03-12 is NOT REPRODUCIBLE — the then-live UniV3 pool quoted 0.999998 that day at block 24,637,909 with unchanged liquidity
